assumptions: The customer's 'login and signup' are auth/login and auth/signup in api group app.
'Every public endpoint' means endpoints tagged public, which endpoint_auth none selects (health, auth/login, auth/signup, newsletter/subscribe; bank-accounts/link needs auth despite the name).
The limit is 20 requests per 60 seconds per IP; the customer gave no number.
Attaching per endpoint rather than to the app API group, so authenticated app endpoints are not rate-limited by accident.
redis.ratelimit's key/max/ttl parameter names are correct; the dry run accepted the middleware file, which suggests they parse but this was not verified at runtime.
confusions: The kit does not show how to attach a middleware to an endpoint in XanoScript. The skill only says 'attach' and the catalogue's fix_hint says 'attaching per object replaces inherited middleware'. Three forms were refused: middleware = ["rate_limit"] (Invalid kind for middleware - static:text[]), middleware = [{name, kind}] and middleware = [{name, phase}] (both Invalid block: name). I guessed all three and could not find the right one.

The rate_limiting recipe's Build says 'attach middleware rate_limit ... to the API groups holding public endpoints and to the login API group'. Attaching at the group level would also rate-limit every authenticated endpoint in the app group. The recipe does not say whether to attach per endpoint or per group, and the check fix_hint says prefer the API group.

The recipe's Login rule (rules[1]) has only object_kinds and middleware, filled with api_groups. Scoped to the app group it covers every app endpoint, not only login and signup. I added paths: ["auth"] to narrow it. The recipe does not say that.
The brief gives no guidance on whether a rate_limit middleware should key on $auth.id after login; the recipe mentions both and I used IP only.

The push guard hook blocked 'xano workspace push --help' (only the exact dry-run command is allowed), so I could not read the push flags from help. Not a problem for the task, but the guard's allow-list is narrower than the brief's list.

The XanoScript syntax of redis.ratelimit (key, max, ttl names and the error it raises), with an example middleware file.
A recipe note on per-endpoint versus per-API-group attachment, and the trade-off when the group also holds authenticated endpoints.
A recipe rule that scopes the login rule to the login and signup endpoints by path, rather than the whole API group.
